units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
Mr Tanner wishes to see you, sir.
units.name: THE MAID

units.text: Mr Tanner!
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: Jack!
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: How dare Mr Tanner call on me! Say I cannot see him.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: hurt.
I am sorry you are turning my friend from your door like that.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: calmly.
He's not at the door, sir. He's upstairs in the drawingroom with Miss Ramsden. He came with Mrs Whitefield and Miss Ann and Miss Robinson, sir.
units.name: THE MAID

units.text: Ramsden's feelings are beyond words.
grinning.
That's very like Jack, Mr Ramsden. You must see him, even if it's only to turn him out.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: hammering out his words with suppressed fury.
Go upstairs and ask Mr Tanner to be good enough to step down here.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: The parlormaid goes out; and Ramsden returns to the fireplace, as to a fortified position.
I must say that of all the confounded pieces of impertinence--well, if these are Anarchist manners I hope you like them. And Annie with him! Annie! A--
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: he chokes.
Yes: that's what surprises me. He's so desperately afraid of Ann. There must be something the matter.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Mr John Tanner suddenly opens the door and enters.
He is too young to be described simply as a big man with a beard.
But it is already plain that middle life will find him in that category.

He has still some of the slimness of youth; but youthfulness is not the effect he aims at: his frock coat would befit a prime minister; and a certain high chested carriage of the shoulders, a lofty pose of the head, and the Olympian majesty with which a mane, or rather a huge wisp, of hazel colored hair is thrown back from an imposing brow, suggest Jupiter rather than Apollo.
He is prodigiously fluent of speech, restless, excitable (mark the snorting nostril and the restless blue eye, just the thirty-secondth of an inch too wide open), possibly a little mad.

He is carefully dressed, not from the vanity that cannot resist finery, but from a sense of the importance of everything he does which leads him to make as much of paying a call as other men do of getting married or laying a foundation stone.
A sensitive, susceptible, exaggerative, earnest man: a megalomaniac, who would be lost without a sense of humor.
Just at present the sense of humor is in abeyance.
To say that he is excited is nothing: all his moods are phases of excitement.
He is now in the panic-stricken phase; and he walks straight up to Ramsden as if with the fixed intention of shooting him on his own hearthrug.
But what he pulls from his breast pocket is not a pistol, but a foolscap document which he thrusts under the indignant nose of Ramsden as he exclaims--
Ramsden: do you know what that is?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: loftily.
No, Sir.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: It's a copy of Whitefield's will. Ann got it this morning.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: When you say Ann, you mean, I presume, Miss Whitefield.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: I mean our Ann, your Ann, Tavy's Ann, and now, Heaven help me, my Ann!
units.name: TANNER

units.text: rising, very pale.
What do you mean?
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Mean!
units.name: TANNER

units.text: He holds up the will.
Do you know who is appointed Ann's guardian by this will?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: coolly.
I believe I am.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: You! You and I, man. I! I!! I!!! Both of us!
units.name: TANNER

units.text: He flings the will down on the writing table.
You! Impossible.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: It's only too hideously true.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: He throws himself into Octavius's chair.

Ramsden: get me out of it somehow. You don't know Ann as well as I do. She'll commit every crime a respectable woman can; and she'll justify every one of them by saying that it was the wish of her guardians. She'll put everything on us; and we shall have no more control over her than a couple of mice over a cat.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Jack: I wish you wouldn't talk like that about Ann.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: This chap's in love with her: that's another complication. Well, she'll either jilt him and say I didn't approve of him, or marry him and say you ordered her to. I tell you, this is the most staggering blow that has ever fallen on a man of my age and temperament.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Let me see that will, sir.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: He goes to the writing table and picks it up.
I cannot believe that my old friend Whitefield would have shown such a want of confidence in me as to associate me with--
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: His countenance falls as he reads.

It's all my own doing: that's the horrible irony of it. He told me one day that you were to be Ann's guardian; and like a fool I began arguing with him about the folly of leaving a young woman under the control of an old man with obsolete ideas.
units.name: TANNER
